seoTitle: How to Connect MT4 or MT5 to TradingView
metaDescription: Learn how to bridge TradingView with MetaTrader 4 or 5 using broker connections, third-party connectors, and alert-forwarding tools.
intro: TradingView and MetaTrader are separate ecosystems, so connecting them requires a bridge rather than a built-in native link. This guide walks through the broker setup, third-party connectors, and alert-forwarding tools traders use to synchronize charting on TradingView with execution on MT4 or MT5.

steps.heading: Set up your MetaTrader login
steps.body: Make sure your MT4 or MT5 account is active and properly connected to your broker before attempting any bridge setup.

steps.heading: Set up TradingView's broker bridge
steps.body: If your broker supports it, connect TradingView's built-in broker integration to link charting with your trading account.

steps.heading: Use third-party connector tools
steps.body: Tools like PineConnector or similar bridge services translate TradingView alerts into orders that MT4 or MT5 can execute.

steps.heading: Forward alerts to MetaTrader
steps.body: Configure your TradingView alerts to send signals through the connector service, which then relays them into your MetaTrader terminal.

steps.heading: Verify synchronized execution
steps.body: Test the setup with a small trade to confirm alerts triggered on TradingView are correctly reaching and executing in MT4 or MT5.

faq.question: Can TradingView connect directly to MetaTrader without third-party tools?
faq.answer: In most cases no — since they're separate ecosystems, a bridge tool or connector service is typically needed to link them.

faq.question: Is PineConnector free to use?
faq.answer: Third-party connector tools like PineConnector usually have their own pricing structure, so check the current plans directly with the provider.

faq.question: Does this bridge setup work for both MT4 and MT5?
faq.answer: Yes, most bridge and connector tools support both MT4 and MT5, though setup steps can differ slightly between the two.

faq.question: Is connecting TradingView to MetaTrader risky?
faq.answer: As with any automated execution setup, it's important to test thoroughly with small trades first to confirm the connection behaves as expected before relying on it fully.
